subject: Mutual Action Playbook & stakeholder orientation for Gridly Health
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.in>
To: Samir Rao <samir@gridly.health>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.in>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Playbook & stakeholder orientation for Gridly Health

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum toward your evaluation goals and the end-of-Q2 close you mentioned, I've attached a first draft of a Mutual Action Playbook (MAP) that outlines milestones, stakeholders, and a recommended technical evaluation cadence.

High-level ask from us: please confirm the Gridly engineering point of contact and any compliance contacts who need to be on the distribution for evidentiary requests. Suggested owners from our side are below. If that looks good, I'll send calendar invites for a 60-minute kickoff next week to walk through the timeline and open items.

Redwood proposed internal owners:
- Monica Patel — Account Executive (program owner, schedule / commercial)
- Diego Fernandez — Solutions Engineer (technical lead for integration & perf)
- Maya Srinivasan — ML Engineer (model evaluation & data requirements)

Key MAP milestones (draft):
- Week 0: Kickoff & roles alignment
- Week 1: Data access + sample ingestion test
- Week 2–3: Eval runs and quality review (prompt + dataset)
- Week 4: Cost/latency tuning, quantization validation
- Week 5: Final results + exec review / decision

Attachments: [Attachment: Gridly_MAP_v0.1.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)]

Two quick questions so we can tailor the kickoff agenda:
1) Who from Gridly should attend the technical deep-dive (engineer names + emails)?
2) Any restrictions on sample data sharing or preferred S3/GCS bucket details (or shall we use synthetic samples first)?

Thanks — looking forward to getting things moving.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.in

From: Samir Rao <samir@gridly.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.in>
Cc: Leah Thompson <leah.thompson@gridly.health>, procurement@gridly.health, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.in>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Playbook & stakeholder orientation for Gridly Health

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear outline and the MAP.

Confirming attendees from Gridly for the kickoff:
- Leah Thompson (Engineering Lead) — leah.thompson@gridly.health
- Samir Rao (Product, evaluation owner) — samir@gridly.health
- Procurement (cc'd) for contract/timing visibility

Quick notes / constraints from our side:
- We'd prefer to use a redacted extract of production data for quality tests. I need to confirm with our security team whether we can share an S3 read-only path or if we should upload to a temporary bucket managed by Redwood.
- Primary goals: 1) validate end-to-end latency at P95 with our prompt set, 2) confirm semantic similarity/QA thresholds on retrieval-augmented responses.

Next steps for us: Leah will attend the kickoff and can speak to data ingestion and infra constraints. Can you propose two 60-minute slots next week (PST)? Also, please include the detailed checklist for things Gridly must have ready before the eval.

—Samir
Samir Rao
Director of Product | Gridly Health
samir@gridly.health

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks for confirming. A couple of practical items I want to call out so the kickoff time is maximally productive:

Pre-kickoff checklist (technical) — please review and let us know which items are already in place:
- Access: S3 read-only role or presigned URLs for a sample bucket OR permission to push up test blobs to a temporary Redwood-managed bucket
- Schema: example records (JSON/CSV) + expected fields for retrieval / prompt inputs
- Auth: If Gridly requires a VPC-peered path or private endpoint for evaluation, flag that now (we'll scope time)
- Latency target: any target for P95 / P99 token-level latency that we should optimize for
- Privacy: need to know if output logging is allowed and what obfuscation rules apply

Proposed technical breakout (45 min) during kickoff:
- 0–10 min: architecture & access (who owns what)
- 10–25 min: sample ingestion & quick smoke test plan
- 25–40 min: evaluation metrics, prompts, and pass/fail thresholds
- 40–45 min: risks, next steps, and ownership

Attachments included for reference: [Attachment: data_ingest_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 18 KB)]

I'll be prepared to demo a sample ingestion flow and an eval run if you can provide a small (<=1000 record) sample during kickoff.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.in
